question:
(i) Explain why photons emitted in the hydrogen line spectrum have definite energies.
(ii) A radioactive nucleus may emit gamma radiation of definite energy. Compare this emission with spectral emission from hydrogen.

options.A:
(i) Hydrogen electrons occupy discrete allowed energy levels. A transition from $E_i$ to $E_f$ emits a photon with $h\nu=E_i-E_f$, so its energy and frequency are definite.
(ii) Gamma radiation can also have definite energy when an excited nucleus makes a transition between discrete nuclear energy levels. Hydrogen lines have electronic origin, whereas gamma emission has nuclear origin.
options.B:
(i) Hydrogen photons have arbitrary energies because electrons can occupy any energy between two levels.
(ii) Gamma rays are emitted only by electron transitions outside the nucleus.
options.C:
(i) Definite spectral energies arise because all hydrogen electrons have identical kinetic energy in every orbit.
(ii) Gamma radiation is a continuous spectrum produced by resistance heating.
options.D:
(i) Hydrogen photons are produced when protons move between nuclear levels.
(ii) Gamma photons have no definite energy because nuclear energy levels are continuous.
